references.text: In the next verses, Jesus gives the positive counterpart to the exhortation in verse 12: instead of inviting friends and relatives, one should invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind—those who cannot repay—and you will be rewarded at the resurrection of the righteous ([ref:Luk 14:13-14|Luke 14:13-14]).

Jesus warns against doing good deeds to be seen by people and receive human reward. Instead, one should do good in secret, and the Father who sees in secret will reward you ([ref:Matt 6:1-4|Matthew 6:1-4]). This is the same principle as in Luke 14:12: do not do good to receive repayment.

Jesus says that if you love those who love you, do good to those who do good to you, or lend to those from whom you expect to get something back, you have no credit. Even sinners do the same. You are to love your enemies and do good without expecting anything in return ([ref:Luk 6:32-35|Luke 6:32-35]).
Proverbs exhorts: "Do not say to your neighbor, 'Go, and come again'"—an exhortation to do good without calculation ([ref:Ordsp 3:28|Proverbs 3:28]).
Nehemiah encourages the people to send food to those who have nothing prepared—to share with those who cannot repay ([ref:Neh 8:10-12|Nehemiah 8:10-12]).
The Mosaic law requires Israelites to care for the poor, foreigners, orphans, and widows—that is, to share with those who cannot repay ([ref:5 Mos 14:28-29|Deuteronomy 14:28-29]).

The parable immediately before in the same context deals with not seeking the place of honor at a banquet, but taking the lowest seat. The theme is the same: humility and not seeking human honor or reward ([ref:Luk 14:7-11|Luke 14:7-11]).

Jesus asks: "If you love those who love you, what credit do you have?" Even tax collectors do that. The principle is the same as in Luke 14:12—there is no merit in reciprocal hospitality ([ref:Matt 5:46-47|Matthew 5:46-47]).
Isaiah describes true fasting as sharing bread with the hungry and bringing homeless wanderers into your house—hospitality toward those who cannot repay ([ref:Jes 58:7|Isaiah 58:7]).
